verses.text: There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews:

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Nicodemus was an important man. He was a teacher of the law and a leader of his people. Many of the leaders did not trust Jesus. But Nicodemus had seen enough to want to know more.

verses.text: The same came to Jesus by night, and said unto him, Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that thou doest, except God be with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The same came to Jesus by night, and said unto him,

segments.speaker: nicodemus
segments.text: Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that thou doest, except God be with him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He came at night. Maybe he did not want to be seen. Maybe night was simply when there was quiet enough to talk. Either way, he came with an honest question in his heart.

verses.text: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Nicodemus was a careful thinker, and this made no sense to him.

verses.text: Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?

segments.speaker: nicodemus
segments.text: How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus was not talking about being born again the way a baby is born. He was talking about a new life that comes from God.

verses.text: Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.

verses.text: That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.

verses.text: Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.

verses.text: The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: You cannot see the wind. You cannot tell it where to go. But you hear it moving in the trees, and you know it is there. Jesus said the life God gives is like that.

verses.text: Nicodemus answered and said unto him, How can these things be?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nicodemus answered and said unto him,

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: It is a question many people have asked since. Jesus told him that even a teacher of Israel had more to learn. Then he pointed back to an old story Nicodemus knew well.

verses.text: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:

verses.text: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Long ago in the wilderness, the people of Israel were dying from snakebites. God told Moses to make a serpent of bronze and lift it high on a pole. Whoever looked at it lived. Jesus said he would be lifted up in the same way.

verses.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

verses.text: For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: That is one of the best known verses in the whole Bible, and it was first spoken to one man, in the dark, who came with questions.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: John does not tell us what Nicodemus said that night. But later in the same gospel, he stood up for Jesus among the other leaders. And after the cross, he came again, this time in daylight, carrying spices to help bury the body of Jesus.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Nicodemus started with questions. Jesus did not turn him away for them. He met him in the night and told him about a love big enough for the whole world.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to John 3:1-17; Jesus's words only as scripture; water and Spirit left uninterpreted (no position on baptism); the bronze serpent is Num 21; Nicodemus later is John 7:50 and 19:39; no telling the listener she is saved or lost.

cultural.note: A seeker shown with dignity; questions honoured, not scolded.
